subject.title: Per-agent tools.selfDeny — allow tool inheritance to subagents while denying direct use

question: Should OpenClaw add an explicit per-agent delegate-only/self-deny tool policy, and should that be modeled as tools.selfDeny, delegateOnly, scoped allow entries, or folded into per-spawn toolsAllow work?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the change adds public config surface and changes how security-sensitive tool boundaries flow from requester agents to subagents.

options.title: Approve explicit delegate-only config
options.body: Add an optional per-agent policy that hides tools from the requester model while preserving deny-wins behavior and controlled child inheritance.

options.title: Fold into per-spawn policy
options.body: Let the per-spawn toolsAllow work own child narrowing and document that parent direct-use prevention still requires separate profiles or prompt guidance.

options.title: Keep monotonic policy only
options.body: Reject parent-deny delegation and document the security rationale plus the separate-agent workaround.

recommendation.title: Approve explicit delegate-only config
recommendation.body: Add an optional per-agent policy that hides tools from the requester model while preserving deny-wins behavior and controlled child inheritance.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue history already routes this security-sensitive public config choice through steipete, and the decision is broader than a single code owner line.
